title: code-graph's published default rules name ‹product›'s own functions and SDKs
rawReport:
## Summary
`@demlik/code-graph`'s built-in node-kind rules hardcode names from one consumer's codebase, ‹product›'s: its auth helpers, its payment SDK and its VM-spawn functions. For any other user they're dead weight, and they quietly mislabel any function that happens to share one of those names. #349 already applied this fix to `contracts` (default `[]`). The same treatment is owed to the rest.

## What I was doing
Closing out tickets from the #307 import and PR #349 (the code-graph sync). The #344 operator flagged `"^dodopayments:"`, and reading the file showed the leak is wider and mostly predates #349.

## What I observed
In `packages/code-graph/src/kinds/rules.ts` on main (from the #307 snapshot):
- `authNames` / `authCallees`: `require(…|ScanCredential|ProjectCiBotContext)`, `verify(…|RunnerToken|GithubWebhookSignature)`, `^assertProjectBelongsToOrg$`, `^getUserMembership$`
- `effectDeclarations["vm-spawn"]`: `^(insertGceInstance|spawnCloudRunner|deleteGceHands)$`

PR #349 adds `effectDeclarations["network-call"]: "^dodopayments:"` and `authCallees: "^getSessionFromHeaders$"`.

## Why it matters
Published defaults are a contract: every user of the package gets them. Consumer-specific names are wrong for everyone else, and they hide the fact that the consumer should be configuring them. They'll also keep accreting as ‹product› syncs more work in (#345 is next).

## Pointers
- packages/code-graph/src/kinds/rules.ts (the schema `.default(...)` blocks)
- PR #349, deviation 1 (`contracts` → `[]`), the precedent
- ‹product›'s rules file (where these patterns belong on its side)

## Suggested next step (non-binding)
Keep only framework-generic patterns in the defaults: `fetch`, D1, drizzle, pg, sqlite, R2/KV, Queue, Workflow, `authScopes`, and generic `require(Auth|Session)` / `authorize*`. Document that consumers add their own via the rules file, and put ‹product›'s list in its config when it switches to the package. The mistake-proofing piece: a test that snapshots the default rule set, so any future addition shows up as a reviewed diff instead of slipping in during a sync. Changeset: code-graph minor (defaults narrow). Sequence after #344 merges, since it touches the same file.

enriched:
## Scope (v1)

`@demlik/code-graph`'s published `NodeKindRulesSchema` defaults in `packages/code-graph/src/kinds/rules.ts` include function names from one consumer, ‹product›. Every user of the package gets them. At `origin/main` (9864280):

- `authNames["auth-gate"]` / `authCallees["calls-auth-gate"]`: the `ScanCredential` and `ProjectCiBotContext` alternatives of `require(…)`, the `MachineToken`, `RunnerToken` and `GithubWebhookSignature` alternatives of `verify(…)`, `^assertProjectBelongsToOrg$`, `^getUserMembership$`, `^getSessionFromHeaders$`
- `effectCallees["vm-spawn"]`: `^(insertGceInstance|spawnCloudRunner|deleteGceHands)$`

PR #349 (for #344) adds more in the same blocks (`"network-call": "^dodopayments:"`) and already sets `contracts` to `[]`, which is the precedent this issue follows. This PR narrows the defaults to patterns that name a platform, library or generic convention, and adds a snapshot test so any future addition shows up as a reviewed diff.

Triage note: the blocking edge on #344 exists because both PRs edit the same `.default(…)` blocks. The builder should work against `rules.ts` as #349 leaves it, not the pre-sync copy, and remove whatever consumer-specific names #349 brings in too. Deciding what counts as generic is part of the work. The rule is that a pattern stays only if a codebase that has never seen ‹product› could plausibly match it (`fetch`, D1/drizzle/pg/sqlite verbs, R2/KV, Queue, Workflow, `require(Auth|Session|SessionToken)`, `verify(ApiKey|AccessToken|SharedSecret)`, `authorize*`).

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] No default in `NodeKindRulesSchema` names a ‹product› function, SDK or service. Every name in the list above, and every consumer-specific name #349 adds, is gone. A kind whose only patterns were consumer-specific (e.g. `vm-spawn`) defaults to an empty list or is dropped from the defaults.
- [ ] A test snapshots the full parsed default rule set (`NodeKindRulesSchema.parse({})`), so any change to a default fails until the snapshot is updated in review.
- [ ] A test shows a consumer's rules file can still add the removed patterns back and have them match.
- [ ] `packages/code-graph/README.md` says the defaults are framework-generic only and shows how a consumer adds its own auth, effect and entry names through the rules file.
- [ ] A changeset records a `@demlik/code-graph` minor bump (defaults narrow).
- [ ] `pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm test` pass.

### No-gos

- Do not write ‹product›'s own rules file. That belongs in ‹product›'s repo when it switches to the package.
- Do not change the rules schema's shape or the matching logic. Only defaults change.
- No change to `contracts`. #349 already covers it.
